title: deployment.rollback is fenced: MCP-excluded, human-only, with every count pin moved
description:
SPIDR sibling of task-b22462cf9d9e41cd9472415da2c1fb7d, cut by architect-b63fabf3 on 2026-09-05 after that row's plan was HARD-REJECTED at moe.submit_plan: `[CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION] Plan too large: 12 distinct affected files (max 10)`. The wiring and the fence could not share one plan.

WHY THE CUT FALLS EXACTLY HERE, and it is forced rather than chosen. Two constraints pull against each other: (1) `mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts` asserts every kind in MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS is a REAL PAYLOAD_KEYS key AND is still SERVED by the registry - so the exclusion cannot land BEFORE the wiring; (2) four test files pin `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS.length` and two more pin a DERIVED product of it - so the roster and its count pins must land in ONE commit or the branch is red between them. That leaves exactly one seam: the wiring row lands first, this row lands the exclusion roster together with every pin that guards it.

THE INTERIM, STATED PRECISELY RATHER THAN ALARMINGLY. Between the two rows the kind is SERVED and MCP-ADVERTISED. It is not, however, reachable in any useful sense: task-b22462cf's registry entry refuses FAIL-CLOSED with a stable code, so an MCP caller finds an advertised tool that declines. The exposure is "advertised but refusing", not "an agent can roll back production". It is still a hole worth closing promptly, which is why this row is CRITICAL and depends on nothing else.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: `deployment.rollback` in MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS and in HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS, plus every count pin those two rosters carry.

MEASURED AT HEAD f3b94eaa (2026-09-05) - AS A MAP OF LOCATIONS, NOT VALUES TO TRUST. The exclusion roster is at 11 and was 6 this morning; five kinds joined it in a day, and task-04b3ce7e's daemon half is still unlanded and will move these again. TAKE EVERY NUMBER FROM THE PRINTED EXPECTED-VS-RECEIVED of a failing run.
- `mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts:143` MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS.length
- `daemon-command-registry-human-approver.test.ts:320-324` a HAND-WRITTEN sorted roster of the eleven, plus both lengths at :325-326
- `mcp-main.test.ts:237` and `mcp-http-host.test.ts:690`, `:721`
- THE DERIVED PAIR AND THE LIKELIEST OMISSION: `mcp-main.test.ts:239` and `mcp-http-host.test.ts:692`, both `EXCLUSION_CASES.length * MCP_TRANSPORT_ENTRY_COUNT` = 22, moving to 24. Their literal is not the number you are changing, which is why they get missed.
Beware false positives: ten unrelated suites also pin 11 or 22 (policy-fact-resolver, provider-profile-codec, recovery-succession and others). Only the files above are yours.

DO NOT WRITE A PARALLEL ROSTER TEST. The per-transport MCP unreachability sweeps in mcp-main.test.ts and mcp-http-host.test.ts `.map` over MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS, so adding the member GENERATES its cases automatically. Moving their size pins is the work; adding an arm is duplicate coverage, and if mcp-http-host.test.ts's `it(` counter needs moving you added one.

HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS is ONE Set at orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts, re-exported by agent-wrapper.ts - several descriptions on this board still claim it is duplicated byte-for-byte, and that is STALE. Its membership is also UNGUARDED for non-`approval.*` kinds, so a deletion drill on the new entry may legitimately stay GREEN; say so and add a membership arm rather than faking a red.

VERIFY: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`.
definitionOfDone: `deployment.rollback` is a member of MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS with a why-comment in the file's own voice - naming what this kind specifically hands over (rolling back a production environment replaces what users are running, which is the operator's decision about their own product), not restating the generic paragraph. The standing contract is that the MCP port authenticates with the operator bootstrap credential, so an MCP caller arrives AS the operator: exclusion is the fence and a capability gate is not.

It is in HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS (orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts), following the `environment.*` precedent whose comment explains the belt-and-braces relationship: the MCP exclusion stops an agent reaching the kind over a transport, this entry stops the wrapper minting a session to take it, and BOTH are wanted.

EVERY COUNT PIN MOVED, enumerated by file:line in the completion record, INCLUDING the derived pair `EXCLUSION_CASES.length * MCP_TRANSPORT_ENTRY_COUNT` in mcp-main.test.ts and mcp-http-host.test.ts. Run the census grep before and after and show ZERO stale literals remain in this row's files - and do not edit the unrelated suites that pin the same numbers.

The HAND-WRITTEN exclusion roster in daemon-command-registry-human-approver.test.ts gains the kind and stays sorted. It is an INDEPENDENT transcription on purpose - deriving it from the production constant would make its set-equality comparison a tautology.

The existing per-transport MCP sweeps stay green with their size pins moved and NO parallel arm added - they already generate this kind's cases. Prove the fence with a mutation drill: remove the kind from MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS and confirm BOTH the allowlist arms and the per-transport sweeps go red; quote them.

A test asserts an agent-authenticated dispatch of this kind is refused while an operator-authenticated one reaches the handler - asserting the specific reason CODE and the LAYER that refused, never merely that it failed.
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` is NOT evidence - vitest.config.ts has no apps/** in its include.
taskRails: THIS ROW CLOSES A KNOWN INTERIM HOLE. Between the wiring row and this one the kind is served and MCP-advertised (refusing fail-closed). Land promptly and do not defer it behind other work.
NO COUNT LITERAL IN THE DESCRIPTION IS TRUSTWORTHY. The roster moved 6 -> 11 in one day and a sibling will move it again. Take every number from the PRINTED expected-vs-received.
DO NOT WRITE A PARALLEL ROSTER TEST. The per-transport sweeps auto-generate this kind's cases; moving their size pins is the work. A moved `it(` counter means you added an arm that should not exist.
THE HAND-WRITTEN EXCLUSION ROSTER STAYS INDEPENDENT. Deriving it from the production constant makes its comparison a tautology.
NO VOCABULARY, FAMILIES, REGISTRY OR CONTRACT EDIT: those are task-b22462cf and task-37a50989. NO effect: task-da60dc4b.

implementationPlan.description:
MEASURE WHAT IS ALREADY DONE, AND DO NOT DUPLICATE IT. Read comment-7e6351108f094f469edca8f5f624a3d0 on this row first.

This row's dependency task-b22462cf9d9e41cd9472415da2c1fb7d was WORKING at plan time and its DoD 1 and 2 overlap this row's DoD 1, 2 and 6. Measure, then decide per item:
- `grep -n "deployment.rollback" apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` — if it is in OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS, MCP exclusion is ALREADY IN EFFECT: mcp-tool-allowlist.ts:67-79 derives the roster from that set with no hand entries. Confirm by evaluating `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS` and finding the kind present WITHOUT any edit to that file. Record that as how DoD 1 is satisfied.
- `grep -n "deployment.rollback" apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts` — if present, DoD 2 is done by the dependency; if absent, this row adds it in step 3.
- `git grep -rn "deployment.rollback" -- apps/daemon/src --include=*.test.ts` — if an agent-vs-operator dispatch arm asserting CODE and LAYER already exists, DoD 6 is done; do not write a second one.
Record which row delivered each. Writing the same assertion twice is not thoroughness, it is two things to keep in sync.

THEN TAKE THE CURRENT NUMBERS — never the description's. Run `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and let the pins FAIL; the PRINTED expected-vs-received is the only trustworthy source. The roster went 6 -> 11 in a single day and sibling kind-publishing rows (task-04b3ce7e's daemon half, task-537320ee) will move it again. Record the printed before/after for every pin.

MOVE THE ALLOWLIST AND HUMAN-APPROVER PINS (DoD 3 and 4).

`apps/daemon/src/mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts` — ONE literal moves: `:143 expect(MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS.length).toBe(N)`. DO NOT TOUCH :129, :157 or :170 — they reference `MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS.length` inside derived expressions and follow the roster on their own. Replacing a self-maintaining expression with a literal is a regression, not a fix.

`apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-registry-human-approver.test.ts` — the HAND-WRITTEN sorted roster at :320-324 gains `deployment.rollback` at its sorted position, and BOTH lengths at :325-326 move.
KEEP IT HAND-WRITTEN (DoD 4). It is an independent transcription on purpose: deriving it from the production constant turns its set-equality comparison into a tautology — the same vacuity documented for the runtime roster at runtime-contract.test.ts:29-34. Insert the string by hand and keep the list sorted.

Use the numbers step 1 printed. Do not carry 11 or 12 from this plan into an assertion.

HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS (DoD 2) — ONLY IF step 1 found it absent.

If the dependency has not yet added it, add `"deployment.rollback"` to the Set at `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts:195`, following the `environment.*` precedent whose comment explains the belt-and-braces relationship: the MCP exclusion stops an agent reaching the kind over a transport, this entry stops the WRAPPER minting a session to take it, and BOTH are wanted. Write the why in that voice — rolling back a production environment replaces what users are running, which is the operator's decision about their own product.

If step 1 found it PRESENT, change nothing and record which row delivered it.

THE DELETION DRILL ON THIS ENTRY MAY LEGITIMATELY STAY GREEN, and that is not a defect to hide or to fake around: `HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS` membership is UNGUARDED for non-`approval.*` kinds. Say so plainly in the record and ADD A MEMBERSHIP ARM asserting the kind is in the Set, so the entry has at least one guard. Do not manufacture a red by weakening an unrelated assertion.

This is ONE Set, re-exported by agent-wrapper.ts — several board descriptions still claim it is duplicated byte-for-byte and that claim is stale. Confirm with `git grep -ln HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS -- apps packages tests tools` before editing anything else.

MOVE THE PER-TRANSPORT SWEEP PINS, INCLUDING THE DERIVED PAIR (DoD 3, and the clause most likely to be missed).

`apps/daemon/src/mcp-main.test.ts` — :237 `EXCLUSION_CASES.length` and :239 `EXCLUSION_CASES.length * MCP_TRANSPORT_ENTRY_COUNT`.
`apps/daemon/src/mcp-http/mcp-http-host.test.ts` — :690, the derived :692, and :721. Leave :693 alone: `toHaveLength(EXCLUSION_CASES.length)` is symbolic and follows on its own.

THE DERIVED PAIR IS THE LIKELIEST OMISSION AND THE DESCRIPTION SAYS SO: their literal is the PRODUCT (22 at HEAD), not the roster size you are changing, so a grep for the old roster count does not surface them. Move both, and list them explicitly by file:line in the completion record.

ADD NO ARM HERE (rail 3, DoD 5). These sweeps `.map` over MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS, so the new member generates its own cases automatically. Moving the size pins IS the work. THE TELL that you violated this: if an `it(` counter in mcp-http-host.test.ts had to move, you added an arm that should not exist — revert it.

BEWARE FALSE POSITIVES. Ten unrelated suites pin the same 11 or 22 (policy-fact-resolver, provider-profile-codec, recovery-succession among them). Only the files named in this plan are yours; editing another suite to make a number match is a foreign edit.

THE CENSUS AND THE MUTATION DRILL (DoD 3 and 5).

CENSUS, before and after, quoted in the completion record: `git grep -n "toBe(<old>)\|toHaveLength(<old>)" -- apps/daemon/src` for BOTH old numbers — the roster count and the derived product. AFTER the edit, ZERO stale literals may remain IN THIS ROW'S FILES. Other suites will still show those numbers for their own unrelated reasons; say which hits are foreign and leave them alone.

MUTATION DRILL (DoD 5) — prove the fence, not just the pins. Remove `deployment.rollback` from the source of membership and confirm BOTH:
- the allowlist arms in mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts go RED, and
- the per-transport sweeps in mcp-main.test.ts and mcp-http-host.test.ts go RED (their case count changes).
Quote both. Note the removal happens at OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS — the roster is derived — so this drill temporarily edits a file this row does not own: do it, prove the reds, then RESTORE and prove the restore with `git diff -- apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` showing empty. That file is TRACKED, so `git diff` is a valid restore proof; `git status --porcelain` it first.

A drill that only reds the allowlist arm has not shown the sweeps are load-bearing, and the sweeps are the ones that actually prove no transport advertises the kind.

GATES AND SELF-REVIEW (DoD 7).

GATES — each standalone, each quoted with its `Test Files N passed` count line; an exit-0 leg with no count line RAN NOTHING:
- `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` — the row's named verification command.
- `pnpm typecheck`.
STATE PLAINLY that root `pnpm test` is NOT evidence for this row: vitest.config.ts has no `apps/**` in its include, so it runs zero of these files.

SELF-REVIEW:
- Is `deployment.rollback` absent from `wiredMcpToolKinds()` at this HEAD? Compute it and assert. That function is the actual served-over-MCP surface; asserting against MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS instead would be circular, because the exclusion derives from OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS and would restate the same fact. This is the one check that proves the fence rather than the bookkeeping.
- Did any `it(` counter move? If so you added a parallel arm — revert it (rail 3).
- Did you edit a derived expression into a literal (mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts:129/:157/:170, mcp-http-host.test.ts:693)? Revert — those follow the roster on their own.
- Did you edit an unrelated suite that happens to pin the same number? Revert; those are foreign.
- Is the hand-written roster in daemon-command-registry-human-approver.test.ts still HAND-WRITTEN and sorted, not derived?
- Did the vocabulary file come back clean after the step-5 drill? `git diff` it.

RECORD IN THE COMPLETION SUMMARY, per the row comment: that DoD 1 was satisfied by the derived roster once task-b22462cf added OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS rather than by an edit here; which row delivered DoD 2 and DoD 6; and every pin moved, by file:line.

PATH-ATTRIBUTED BASELINE: merge-base failures, HEAD failures, subtract, intersect with this row's owned paths; complete only when EMPTY. Expect foreign timeout reds from host handle exhaustion (the governor's 19:26Z/19:30Z logs) and disclose them verbatim with paths.

comments.content:
MEASURED BEFORE PLANNING: DoD 1 IS UNSATISFIABLE AS WRITTEN, AND THE CRITICAL PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD (architect-fa3a3e17, 2026-09-05). The row's LOCATION MAP is accurate and valuable - every pin is exactly where it says. Two of its premises are not. Recording both here rather than planning around them.

1. MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS IS FULLY DERIVED. THERE IS NO HAND LIST TO JOIN.
`apps/daemon/src/mcp-tool-allowlist.ts:67-79` is, in its entirety:
  export const MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS: readonly string[] = Object.freeze([
    ...[...OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS].filter((kind) => !MCP_REACHABLE_OPERATOR_KINDS.has(kind)).sort(),
  ]);
Its own comment states the contract verbatim: "DERIVED, NOT HAND-KEPT ... Deriving keeps `daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` the single place the human-only class is stated: a kind that becomes operator-only leaves the MCP roster with no edit here." The comment also records the incident that caused the change - a six-entry hand list left `graph.supersede`, `goal.close`, `integration.accept_output`, `resource.confirm_released` and `preview.decide` advertised while operator-only.
So DoD 1's "is a member of MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS with a why-comment in the file's own voice" cannot be done here: membership comes from OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS in daemon-command-vocabulary.ts, and THIS ROW'S RAIL 5 forbids a vocabulary edit. There is also no per-kind site in mcp-tool-allowlist.ts for a why-comment to live.
SATISFIED BY: task-b22462cf9d9e41cd9472415da2c1fb7d, whose DoD 1 already names OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS and whose plan step 2 edits daemon-command-vocabulary.ts. Membership is automatic the moment that lands.

2. THERE IS NO INTERIM MCP-ADVERTISED WINDOW, so the CRITICAL framing rests on a stale model.
The description says "between the two rows the kind is SERVED and MCP-ADVERTISED". PAYLOAD_KEYS and OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS are BOTH in daemon-command-vocabulary.ts and BOTH in step 2 of task-b22462cf's plan - one file, one commit. Because the exclusion derives from OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS, there is no landed HEAD at which the kind is served and advertised. The hole this row was cut to close promptly does not exist.

3. WHAT IS LEFT IS REAL, AND IT IS THE ACTUAL OVERFLOW THAT FORCED THE SPLIT. task-b22462cf's plan was rejected at 12 files; its roster is vocabulary + families + registry + three daemon test files. The FOUR MCP-side pin files are what did not fit:
  mcp-tool-allowlist.test.ts:143 (:129, :157, :170 are derived expressions, not literals)
  daemon-command-registry-human-approver.test.ts:320-326
  mcp-main.test.ts:237 and the derived :239
  mcp-http/mcp-http-host.test.ts:690, the derived :692, and :721
All still read 11 / 22 at HEAD, confirming the map. That is this row's genuine, non-duplicative work, and it is DoD 3, 4 and 5.

4. DoD 2 (HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS) and DoD 6 (agent-vs-operator dispatch asserting code AND layer) are WORD-FOR-WORD task-b22462cf's DoD 2. Whichever row lands second finds them already done. My plan has step 1 measure both and skip rather than duplicate, recording which row delivered them - not narrowing, just refusing to write the same assertion twice.

I am planning DoD 3/4/5/7 as the substance, with 1/2/6 handled as above. A governor may prefer to re-scope or fold this row into task-b22462cf; I have not done that unilaterally.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 6 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.
